transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is... I just have this constant restless feeling. It's like I’m wound too tight, and I just can’t fully settle down. It happens even when I’m supposed to be doing something quiet, like calmly sitting through a planning meeting for work, or even on my own time when I'm trying to relax by painting or doing yoga. I just can't seem to shake that feeling.
Do these restless feelings come in sudden intense episodes?

No, not really. It's not like a sudden wave that just hits me out of nowhere or anything like that. It's more of a... well, just a constant, steady background feeling. I'm just always a little bit keyed up, rather than having it happen in intense bursts.
Do you find it hard to control the worrying that goes along with this restless feeling?

Um, I wouldn't really say I'm worrying. It's not like my mind is spinning about things going wrong, or... or that I'm anxious about my job or anything like that. It's really just that physical feeling of being keyed up. So, no, I don't really have a problem with worrying along with it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
No, not at all. My mood is actually fine. I haven't felt sad or down or anything like that... it really is just that physical restless feeling I mentioned.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or up compared with your normal self?

No, not really. I don't think I've ever felt unusually energized or... or on some kind of high, if that's what you mean. My overall energy stays pretty steady. It really is just that constant fidgety, keyed-up feeling I always have, rather than any kind of unusual burst of energy or feeling overly up.
Did you have this same kind of restless, fidgety feeling when you were a child?

Yes, I did. I remember back in elementary school, I'd actually get notes sent home to my parents about it. It was usually because I kept popping out of my seat, or talking over my classmates. I also had a habit of rushing to answer things before the teacher even finished asking the question. So, yeah, it's definitely been around since I was a kid.
Does this restlessness cause problems for you at work?

Yes, it does. Because I get so restless, I tend to rush through things, which has led to some mistakes with my purchase orders. Now my planning coordinator has to do extra reviews of my work just to catch those corrections. 

And it's not just at work, actually. It spills over into my personal life, too. At home, family dinners can get a bit tense because... well, my family feels like I'm always talking over them.
